title: One-sample z-test
intro: Known population σ only. Choose the alternative before you compare p with α.

chapters.title: Choose the left tail and run
Read z, p and the decision

beats.spoken: A normal population has known standard deviation four. Test whether its mean is below fifty using an independent sample.
beats.coach: H₀: μ = 50; Hₐ: μ < 50. The population is normal, its standard deviation is known, and the sample is independent.

beats.spoken: Use a z test because the population standard deviation is known. Choose the less-than alternative before seeing the test result.
beats.coach: Known population σ = 4 calls for a z test. Decide on the left-sided alternative and α = 0.05 before you inspect the result.

beats.spoken: The independent observations are already in column A. Open the one-sample z Test.
beats.coach: Column A already contains the list readings. From Lists & Spreadsheet: Menu → 4 Statistics → 4 Stat Tests → 1 z Test.

beats.spoken: Choose Data because the individual readings are already in a named list.
beats.coach: Individual readings are available, so keep Data in the input-method dialog and press Enter.

beats.spoken: Enter the null mean fifty and the known population standard deviation four. Then choose readings for List.
beats.coach: Enter μ₀ = 50 and σ = 4, then choose the named list readings. Tab moves between fields.

beats.spoken: Keep frequency at one. Change the alternative to less than. Leave the optional graph unchecked.
beats.coach: Keep Frequency List = 1. Choose μ < μ₀, leave Draw unchecked and press Enter.

beats.spoken: Under the null hypothesis, the chance of a z score of negative three or lower is about zero point zero zero one three five. The test counted nine observations from the list.
beats.coach: The LCD counts n = 9 and shows z = −3. The one-tailed p-value is about 0.00135.

beats.spoken: There is evidence that the mean is below fifty. A two-sided alternative would use both tails.
beats.coach: p ≈ 0.00135 < 0.05. Reject H₀: there is evidence that μ is below 50. A two-sided alternative would use both tails.
